module

public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Limits
public import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Scheme
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.MvPolynomial.Homogeneous

@[expose] public section

-- The contents of this file will be in mathlib as of #26061

universe u v
open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial AlgebraicGeometry

variable (n : Type v) (S : Scheme.{max u v})

local notation "ℤ[" n "]" => homogeneousSubmodule n ℤ
local notation3 "ℤ[" n "].{" u "," v "}" => homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{max u v} ℤ)

attribute [local instance] MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra

/--
The projective space over a scheme `S`, with homogeneous coordinates indexed by `n`
-/
noncomputable def ProjectiveSpace : Scheme.{max u v} :=
  pullback (terminal.from S) (terminal.from (Proj ℤ[n].{u, v}))

/-- `ℙ(n; S)` is the affine `S` indexed by `n` -/
scoped [AlgebraicGeometry] notation "ℙ("n"; "S")" => ProjectiveSpace n S

findings.description: The notation's docstring at line 42 says “ℙ(n; S) is the affine S indexed by n”, but the notation expands to ProjectiveSpace n S, the projective-space construction. For example, ℙ(Fin 2; Spec ℂ) is the projective line, not affine space. The definition and its problem-file use are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: The Stacks Project, Definition 27.13.2 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ND), defines projective space over S by base-changing Proj(ℤ[T₀,…,Tₙ]) to S. This is the construction used by ProjectiveSpace.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the notation docstring with “ℙ(n; S) is the projective space over S with homogeneous coordinates indexed by n”, or inherit ProjectiveSpace's docstring.

reformulations.difference: The definition uses pullbacks of maps to the chosen terminal scheme, rather than explicitly naming Spec ℤ as the base; its coefficient ring is a universe-lifted copy of ℤ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib's specULiftZIsTerminal proves that Spec(ULift ℤ) is terminal, and ULift.ringEquiv identifies the coefficient ring with ℤ. Transporting the pullback along the terminal-object isomorphism gives the usual fibre product over Spec(ULift ℤ). In /workspace/review/isos.lean I constructed this isomorphism, proved that it commutes with the projection to S, and proved the resulting ↔ between the two isomorphism-class descriptions. Thus this is exactly the standard base-change construction, not a different product.

reformulations.difference: The cited MathOverflow formulation asks for a direct sum of two line bundles. The Lean conclusion instead asks for a Splitting (Fin 2), whose two summands are required not to be isomorphic to the original bundle.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On the nonempty scheme ℙⁿ_ℂ, ranks of these finite constant-rank bundles are invariant under isomorphism and additive under direct sum. The summand ranks therefore add to 2. A rank-zero summand is the zero bundle and would make the other summand isomorphic to the original bundle, violating Splitting.non_trivial. Both summands consequently have rank 1. Conversely, two rank-one summands cannot be isomorphic to a rank-two bundle and give precisely such a splitting. The coordinate index Fin (n + 1) correctly denotes ℙⁿ, not ℙⁿ⁺¹.

review.notes: No mathematical defect was found in the library construction or its projective-space interpretation at the sole problem-file use. Checked both local notations, the ordinary degree-one grading, universe lifting, and empty/singleton/infinite coordinate conventions. Lean experiments in scratch.lean, nonempty.lean, and isos.lean all compile: they verify empty-coordinate and empty-base cases, nonemptiness of Proj over ℤ with a nonempty coordinate type, basic grading cases, and the base-change equivalence. The pinned Mathlib has no duplicate scheme-theoretic ProjectiveSpace; its linear-algebraic Projectivization is a different, appropriate notion. The reviewed file's checksum matches the requested commit, and no repository files were edited.
